task: Library audit (component lint, token bindings, variant checks)
why: Long mechanical MCP runs; thoroughness, not deep reasoning

task: Variable/style existence audit
why: Deterministic key lookups

task: Two-file diff (fork vs master, duplication check)
why: Hashing and comparison live in scripts; what's left is procedure discipline (identity checks, stability re-runs) and saying what each difference means

task: Contrast matrix / ratios grid
why: Pure WCAG math + structured writes

task: Documentation generation / regeneration
why: Mirrors library data into tables

task: Tokens mapping example tables
why: Skill-guided, repeatable

task: Properties table for a component page
why: Draws the rows the snapshot's own walk reads from the open file; the component decides the content

task: Writing component descriptions
why: Structured short-form prose against a recorded per-project shape. Step up where the judgement is *boundary* work — whether a component is one thing or two, whether a child is slot-only

task: OKLCH scale generation (standard)
why: Rule-following once the method is defined

task: Brand-color anchoring problems, ramps failing contrast
why: Genuine judgment and trade-offs

task: Capturing a project's conventions
why: Read-only, but the output is what **every** later run hydrates from, so an error propagates instead of surfacing. Its hard parts are exactly the escalation triggers below: ambiguous convention calls, contradictory evidence, and knowing when to leave `[TBD]` rather than infer

task: Full component pass (audit + properties + descriptions)
why: Multi-stage autonomy; model must catch its own mistakes

task: Creating or revising skills/plugins
why: One-time design decisions that compound; bad skills fail silently forever

task: Validating Figma components for a target platform (web, iOS, Android) before the build
why: The detectors are a tested script per target; what is left is reading each hit against the context document and the target's reference, and putting Figma / code / accept to the designer. Step up only when a finding's class is new to the reference, or a framework's own constraints must be read on top of the platform set

task: File-level audit (page order, names across the library, part prefixes)
why: The checks live in a tested script; what is left is judging whether a flagged component is really a part

task: Whole-project audit (every audit into one record and dashboard)
why: Sequencing only; each stage carries its own reasoning

task: Setting up or reading a design–code parity loop (snapshot, specs, stories, gates)
why: The scripts are written per project against a contract, and each waiver or gate decision is a ruling that outlives the session; reading a red report is Sonnet work once the loop exists

task: Building a front end from a design (HTML/Sass/tokens)
why: Implementation against a design that already decided the hard parts; step up where the *architecture* is the question — stylesheet structure, theming strategy, breakpoint model

task: Composing a screen or flow in Figma from the library, and routing feedback on it
why: Carried from frontend-build's row, which covered it until the 2026-11-11 split; not yet measured on its own

task: Light design systems research (few searches, cited answer)
why: Quick synthesis

task: Deep research (Research feature, many sources)
why: Broad multi-source synthesis earns the premium

task: Long-form docs prose, guides, narrative writing
why: Tuned for long-form generation

task: Editing prose to remove AI tells
why: A rewriting job, which is what Fable is tuned for. The mechanical tells are handled by its scanner, so what is left is judgement about register and about which hits are quoted rather than used. Step up only when the source is dense technical prose where a wrong "simplification" would change a claim
